newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks rebound, helped by Greenspan remark.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks rebound, helped by Greenspan remark.

text.p: Japanese stocks bounced back sharply on Friday, turning around the previous day's decline of over 2.5 percent.
Massive short-covering was triggered by a comment by U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan that Japan is overly pessimistic about its economy.
But brokers said the day's rally could be temporary, and that the flip did not mean the market had started a long-term rising trend.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended up 465.97 points or 2.61 percent at 18,330.01. Its March futures rose 480 to 18,340.
